metadata.title: Anthropic's new Claude product drop just sent a message to these 3 tech stocks

content.text:
On the eve of its much-hyped IPO, Anthropic (ANTH.PVT) is sending its latest message to the software space: We want a large piece of your business… in part to justify our exorbitant valuation.
Coinciding with its roadshow launch, Anthropic released several new features late Tuesday, including Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta. It also pushed Claude Dashboards to general availability as Claude Data. The tools are available on all paid plans and extend Anthropic's efforts to bring more functionality directly within Claude.
The unveiling sent Microsoft (MSFT) shares down 2.2% amid fears of a true new rival to the tech giant's Office franchise.
"There is no question given Anthropic's unprecedented growth, deep technical expertise and substantial financial resources this new product offering bears watching," Stifel analyst Brad Reback wrote to clients. "That said, we do NOT expect these products to have any meaningful impact on M365 growth rates for the foreseeable future based on deep enterprise integration, security/governance and MSFT's complete commitment to ensuring customer IP sovereignty."
Anthropic's release could impact three other tech stocks more quickly than Microsoft, KeyBanc analyst Jackson Ader pointed out. They include Monday.com (MNDY), Asana (ASAN), and Zoom (ZM). All three stocks traded lower on Tuesday amid Anthropic news.
Here's how Ader is thinking through it.
Claude Whiteboards overlaps with Monday.com, Asana, and Zoom.
"Teams can talk through a complex plan, and Claude turns it into a board with deliverables, timelines, assignments, and more for each member of the team," Ader said. "It also competes more directly with Zoom Whiteboard, whose AI capabilities generate diagrams, organize sticky notes, and turn board content into summaries and action items. Where Claude Whiteboards differs from MNDY and ASAN is what happens after the plan is made. The board Claude makes is saved as an artifact. It is not a system of record with the automation, workload views, reporting, and admin controls the work management platforms have. Since a plan has to be run somewhere, MNDY and ASAN will retain their moat for where work gets tracked and executed. A Claude Whiteboard is more of a snapshot, capturing the plan when it's made, but does not stay current on its own as the work moves forward."
Claude Meetings overlaps with AI Notetaker from Monday.com, AI Meetings from Asana, and Zoom's MyNotes and ZoomMate.
"Claude Meetings, which has been marked as 'coming soon' by Anthropic, lets a user add Claude to a call to take notes on the conversation as well as update documents and take actions on behalf of the user regarding items that came up on the call," Ader wrote. "Monday recently launched 'AI Notetaker' and Asana launched 'AI Meetings' where their tools perform similar tasks as Claude Meetings. Join a call, transcribe the conversation, and take action deliverables exiting the meeting. For Zoom, the overlap spans My Notes for transcription, summaries and next steps, built-in Meeting Summary for shared meeting recaps, and ZoomMate for creating deliverables and executing follow-up workflows across connected apps. My Notes already works across Zoom, third-party platforms, and in-person conversations without a meeting bot, so the competitive overlap is in capturing meeting context and turning it into completed work, rather than replacing Zoom's underlying video platform."
